open_points.subject: flow:wait_resume_resolve_cancel / Step 2 (Resume authority source)
open_points.text: State 4 says: "authority checked as it stands at the resume: the unused approval first, then a grant still active; an element whose grant was revoked waits for approval instead (A14 rule 2)." But State 2 A14 rule 2 says: "for a `draft-write` element, the flow activation under which the run started, unless it is a resend after `not_applied`; otherwise its unused approval ..., or a grant still active".
open_points.question: When resuming a `service_unreachable` element of class `draft-write` (not a resend after `not_applied`), which authority must be used?
options: Use flow activation for `draft-write` (except resend after `not_applied`), as A14 rule 2 states.
Use approval/grant order for all classes, as the State 4 resume step states.
open_points.default_guess: Use flow activation for `draft-write` except resend-after-`not_applied`, then use approval/grant.

open_points.subject: flow:start_and_recover_kernel / Step 3 (credential-header collision checks)
open_points.text: State 4 says `check_installed_instances` checks: "no credential header has, case-insensitively, the name of a required header of its instance (A09 rule 1)." But State 2 A09 rule 1 also requires start refusal when credential header matches "a header the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7)".
open_points.question: At startup, must `check_installed_instances` also reject credential-header names that collide with kernel-set headers, not only required headers?
options: Check collisions against both required headers and kernel-set headers.
Check only collisions against required headers.
open_points.default_guess: Reject collisions against both required headers and kernel-set headers.
